chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub and Ali ibn al-Husayn and others narrated to me from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom, is the Ziyarah of al-Rida better or the Ziyarah of Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him)?' He replied: 'The Ziyarah of my father is better. And that is because Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) is visited by all people, but my father is visited only by the special ones from among the Shia.'

key_terms.زِيَارَةُ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Ziyarah of Abu Abdillah (visitation to Imam al-Husayn)
key_terms.زِيَارَةُ الرِّضَا: Ziyarah of al-Rida (visitation to Imam Musa al-Kadhim, known as al-Rida)

ai.seo_question: Why is the Ziyarah of Imam al-Husayn considered superior to that of Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (a.s.) distinguishes between the universal appeal of Imam al-Husayn’s martyrdom, which draws all humanity, and the esoteric, exclusive devotion of the Shia to his own shrine. This hierarchy reflects the Shia theological concept of *khawas* (the elite) who possess deeper spiritual insight, positioning the Imam’s visitation as a specialized act of devotion rather than a general commemoration.
